name: Seeking the Kor Gem
summary: You cross the sea to Darkshore in search of a Kor gem for Jordan Stilwell. Thundris Windweaver sends an Alliance paladin initiate into Blackfathom Deeps, where naga corrupt the potent stone. Jordan needs it for his craft.

sections.title: A Trusted Alliance
sections.body: Paladins in training cross continental borders to Darkshore for materials needed by the human smith Jordan Stilwell. In Auberdine, the night elf Thundris Windweaver remembers the blacksmith with respect. Night elves keep their distance, and some fallen humans have betrayed their trust, yet Thundris still believes paladins can follow a righteous path. He tells them where ancient gems can be found.

sections.title: Into the Deeps
sections.body: Blackfathom Deeps lies beneath the foggy northwestern coast of Ashenvale. Twilight's Hammer cultists and treacherous sea-dwellers inhabit its submerged halls. Naga priestesses there channel foul magic through ancient Kor gems. The gem you seek is deep within the temple complex, amid its dark halls and dangerous inhabitants.

sections.title: Cleansing the Stone
sections.body: When you return a corrupted Kor gem to Thundris Windweaver, he must remove the darkness before Jordan Stilwell can forge it into a holy weapon. The naga give the gem raw magical potency, but twist its enchantment toward evil. Thundris cleanses that corruption so the gem's power stays pure and stable for the sacred smithing ritual ahead.

faq.q: Who sends you to find the Kor Gem?
aliases: who gives seeking the kor gem
faq.answer: Thundris Windweaver, a night elf in Auberdine's coastal port in Darkshore, sends paladins to find the Kor Gem. He acts on behalf of the weaponsmith Jordan Stilwell.

faq.q: Where is the Kor Gem located?
faq.answer: The Kor Gem is inside Blackfathom Deeps, an ancient underground temple on Ashenvale's northwestern coast. Naga priestesses living among the ruins carry the gems.

faq.q: Why does Jordan Stilwell need a Kor Gem?
faq.answer: Jordan Stilwell needs the Kor Gem's potent magic as a material for crafting his refined weapon during the paladin trial The Test of Righteousness.

faq.q: Why does Thundris have to purify the gem?
faq.answer: Naga imbue Kor gems with substantial arcane power, but their foul enchantments taint it. Thundris purifies the gem so its remaining strength can safely serve in a weapon of the Light.

faq.q: Why does Thundris mention a 'fallen kind'?
faq.answer: Thundris likely means human betrayals such as Prince Arthas Menethil's fall into darkness, which tarnished the Silver Hand's reputation across Azeroth. Even so, he judges each paladin on their own merit.

faq.q: Do I need a group to get the Kor Gem?
faq.answer: Thundris warns adventurers not to go alone. Elite naga deep within Blackfathom Deeps carry the gem, so a dedicated adventuring party is strongly advised.

angles.text: As a paladin of the Alliance, you face a trial of character and endurance. It tests your willingness to travel into the hostile depths of Kalimdor to help forge a consecrated arm of the Light.
As a night elf, you see Thundris Windweaver build a fragile but growing bridge between the ancient Kaldorei and the newly allied followers of the Holy Light from the Eastern Kingdoms.
As a member of the Alliance, you see a human blacksmith rely on night elf wisdom and dwarven steel to craft arms against rising darkness.
